data.title: Adjunctive everolimus therapy for treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures associated with tuberous sclerosis (EXIST-3): a phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
data.authors: French JA; Lawson JA; Yapici Z; Ikeda H; Polster T; Nabbout R; Curatolo P; de Vries PJ; Dlugos DJ; Berkowitz N; Voi M; Peyrard S; Pelov D; Franz DN

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Humans: 366 patients aged 2-65 with TSC and treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures on 1-3 antiepileptic drugs; phase 3 RCT, placebo vs low-exposure (trough 3-7 ng/mL) vs high-exposure (9-15 ng/mL) everolimus; 99 centres, 25 countries
data.finding: EXIST-3 was a phase 3, double-blind trial in 366 patients aged 2 to 65 with tuberous sclerosis complex and focal seizures that had not responded to standard drugs. They were randomised 1:1:1 to placebo (n=119), everolimus dosed to a low blood trough of 3-7 ng/mL (n=117) or a high trough of 9-15 ng/mL (n=130), added to their existing antiepileptic drugs. For the primary endpoint, at least a 50% fall in seizure frequency during the 12-week maintenance period, the response rate was 15.1% with placebo, 28.2% with low exposure (p=0.0077) and 40.0% with high exposure (p<0.0001); median seizure reduction was 14.9%, 29.3% and 39.6%. Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 11%, 18% and 24%, and serious adverse events in 3%, 14% and 14% of patients, respectively. The result showed a dose-dependent effect of mTOR inhibition on seizures in TSC, beyond its known effect on TSC tumours. Boundary: patients with TSC and treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures already on 1-3 antiepileptic drugs; comparator was placebo add-on; 18-week core phase (6-week titration, 12-week maintenance), so long-term durability is not addressed here.
data.abstract_excerpt: Everolimus, a mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitor, has been used for various benign tumours associated with tuberous sclerosis complex. We assessed the efficacy and safety of two trough exposure concentrations of everolimus, 3-7 ng/mL (low exposure) and 9-15 ng/mL (high exposure), compared with placebo as adjunctive therapy for treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures in tuberous sclerosis complex.

extracted_findings.intervention: Adjunctive everolimus at trough 3-7 or 9-15 ng/mL vs placebo
extracted_findings.effect: Seizure frequency reduced, dose-dependently (responder rate 15.1% placebo, 28.2% low, 40.0% high exposure)
